name: Settlement Permit (C Permit / Niederlassungsbewilligung)

requirements.blocker_text: This requires 10 years continuous residence for third-country nationals with no settlement treaty (last 5 uninterrupted on a B permit).
This requires A2 oral / A1 written in a national language for the ordinary (10-year) grant.
requirements.fix_path: Take an approved language test at A2 oral / A1 written.

requirements.blocker_text: This 5-year fast track applies to nationals of countries with a bilateral settlement/establishment treaty with Switzerland (commonly Austria, Belgium, Denmark, France, Germany, Greece, Italy, Liechtenstein, Netherlands, Portugal, Spain), plus US and Canadian nationals via long-standing administrative practice — NOT a blanket EU/AFMP entitlement.
This requires B1 oral / A1 written — a higher discretionary bar in exchange for the shorter residence period.
requirements.fix_path: Take an approved language test at B1 oral / A1 written.

evidence_required.document: 5 or 10 years of continuous residence evidence

outcome.duration_length: indefinite; the physical card is reissued every 5 years administratively

sources.title: Settlement permit C - State Secretariat for Migration

notes: GENUINE NATIONALITY-DEPENDENT STRUCTURE, one of the most consequential cross-country findings in the whole dataset for a single route: the residence period is 5 or 10 years depending SPECIFICALLY on the applicant's nationality via bilateral settlement treaties (or, for the US and Canada, long-standing administrative practice rather than a treaty) — NOT a blanket EU/AFMP-wide rule, a common tier-3 misconception this file is built specifically to correct. The 5-year treaty track requires a HIGHER language bar (B1 oral vs A2 for the standard 10-year route) — a genuine and real trade-off, shorter residence in exchange for a tougher language test, worth surfacing prominently. Indefinite status once granted; the physical card itself is reissued every 5 years but this is purely administrative, not a renewal of the underlying status. leads to near-equal labour-market status and strong protection against revocation, comparable in substance to the most generous PR-hub routes elsewhere in this dataset.
